The bull case rests on a record quarter, with revenue of $1.85 billion, up 36.54% on a year earlier, net income of $397 million, up 107.85%, and diluted earnings per share of $2.82, up 63.95% and 30.56% ahead of the estimate of $2.16 [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87% and net margin 21.51%, and revenue was 7.51% higher than in the preceding quarter [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group raised revenue 43.09% to $1.35 billion and operating income 86.18% to $458 million, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group raised revenue 21.60% to $501 million and operating income 68.48% to $155 million, lifting total segment operating income 97.01% to $461 million [D1]. Management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, approximately 37% growth at the mid-point, and earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on about 172 million diluted shares [D1]. On the call, management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply, expected orders to be slightly up from the third quarter, and described a record pipeline [D3]. Commercial communications delivered its first $1 billion quarter and wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time, with wireline orders more than doubling [D3]. The company added nearly 3,000 new customers year to date and sees the 6G opportunity as larger than the 5G cycle [D4]. At the next report the bull case needs to see revenue inside the $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion range, earnings per share inside $3.34 to $3.40, and evidence that supply rather than demand remains the binding constraint on conversion [D3].

The bear case is that these results set a bar the multiple already discounts, with the shares at 45.89 times trailing earnings per share of $7.38 against a forward multiple of 20.66 [D1]. Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear, and the company said supply will govern its ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, leaving a high comparison bar [D3]. The wireline mix has shifted toward manufacturing and direct hyperscaler exposure is limited, so the incremental revenue carries a different margin profile than the historical base [D3]. The company carried net debt of $141 million into the quarter even after generating free cash flow of $403 million [D1]. Analysts on the call pressed on whether demand is sustainable and whether the guidance is capped by supply, and the tone of questioning was more pressing than celebratory [D3]. Published commentary on the quarter argued that the valuation leaves little room for error, and separate research holds that Wall Street price targets are inflated and rarely indicate where a stock is heading [D5]. At the next report the bear case needs to see revenue at the low end of the $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion range or earnings per share at the low end of $3.34 to $3.40, a further quarter in which supply is described as the governor, and margins that hold once the non-repeating tariff benefit is excluded [D3].
